building.name: Michigan Building Code (2021 International Building Code with Michigan amendments, Mich. Admin. Code R 408.30401 to R 408.30499a)
building.local_amendments_note: The state code applies in every Michigan city (MCL 125.1508a(1)); Grand Rapids enforces it through Building Inspections at the Development Center. Grand Rapids City Code Chapter 131 (the chapter the city's fee schedule cites as authority for building permit fees) was not read: Municode answers automated requests with HTTP 403.
building.quote: Building Code 2021 Michigan Building Code - Current Code -Effective April 9, 2025
building.statewide_quote: (1) This act and the code apply throughout the state.
building.city_page_quote: We review plans to make sure proposed construction complies with current codes. Michigan bases its construction codes on standards published by the International Code Council (ICC) and updates them every 3 years. The Michigan Building Code (MBC) covers all types of commercial construction. Grand Rapids ordinances and policies apply to other aspects of development.
building.city_page_note: The city's site names no edition on any page opened. Its former page 'Codes Enforced by Building Inspections' (https://www.grandrapidsmi.gov/Government/Departments/Development-Center/Codes-Enforced-by-Building-Inspections) now returns 404; search-result excerpts of that removed page listed the 2015 Michigan Building Code and the 2021 Michigan Mechanical and Plumbing Codes, i.e. it predated the state's April 9, 2025 change. The city's Commercial Building Plan Review checklist (PDF) still cites 'MBC 2009'. The state's code page is the source for the edition.

fixtures.basis: Michigan's construction code, including the plumbing code's toilet-count table (R 408.30758), applies throughout the state under MCL 125.1508a(1). The city's pages opened (commercial permit overview, renovation guide, plumbing permit page, plumbing plan checklist, building plan review attachment form) refer only to the Michigan codes; the attachment form asks 'Will 13 or more plumbing fixtures required by MPC be modified or added?'. No Grand Rapids ordinance changing the counts was found in two web searches. Grand Rapids City Code Chapter 131 was not read. The state pack's counts stand.

permit.exempt_list_quote: 105.2. Work exempts from permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of the code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of the code or other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction. Permits shall not be required for the following: (a) Building permits shall not be required for the following: (i) One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, if the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet, 11 square meters. (ii) A fence that is not more than 7 feet, 2-meters-134-millimeters, high. (iii) Oil derricks. (iv) A retaining wall that is not more than 4 feet, 1,219 millimeters, in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding class I, II, or III-A liquids. (v) A water tank supported directly on grade if the capacity is not greater than 5,000 gallons, 18,925 liters, and the ratio of height to diameter or width is not greater than 2 to 1. (vi) A sidewalk and driveway not more than 30 inches, 762 millimeters, above adjacent grade and not over any basement or story below and are not part of an accessible route. (vii) Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops, and similar finish work. (viii) Temporary motion picture, television, and theater stage sets and scenery. (ix) Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a group R-3 occupancy [...] (x) Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes, not including service systems. (xi) Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached 1- and 2-family dwellings. (xii) Window awnings in group R-3 and U occupancies [...] (xiii) Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters, and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches, 1,753 millimeters, in height. [(b) electrical and (c) mechanical items follow]
permit.source_note: This is the state rule R 408.30409 (Michigan Building Code section 105.2 as amended), re-read today in the LARA rules file; Grand Rapids enforces it. R 408.30406a (section 105.1) begins: 'Owners or their authorized agents shall obtain the required permit from the building official before undertaking any construction, enlargement, alteration, repair, relocation, demolition, change of occupancy [...]'. The city publishes no exempt-work list of its own for commercial buildings on the pages opened.
permit.city_quote: Planning a renovation of your commercial or 3+ unit building? You will need a commercial building permit. [...] NOTE: Commercial building projects always require either an architect or engineer.
permit.city_quote_2: If you're unsure whether your project needs board or commission approval, ask the Development Center. [...] If your renovations are limited to an interior tenant fit-out or remodeling project and you don't have any questions, you can skip to Preparing your construction plans.
permit.city_home_guide_quote: For houses only (home renovation overview): 'If you're only ripping up carpet, adding a tile backsplash, or painting a room, you don't need one.' Not used on the page: it is about homes.
permit.note: The state list names 'cabinets, countertops, and similar finish work' and 'nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters, and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches'. Toilet partitions or compartments are not named; the only partitions named are nonfixed, movable ones. The city's page says a renovation of a commercial building needs a commercial building permit and does not say what counts as a renovation.

restrooms_city.note: None found. The city's Human Rights Ordinance (City Code Chapter 175, Sections 9.935 to 9.953, in effect December 1, 2019; full text read at https://media-002-us.cdn.govstack.com/grandrapidsmi-us/media/bhslcgya/hro-full.pdf) bars discrimination in public accommodations on the basis of protected classes; the words restroom, bathroom, toilet and locker do not appear in it, and it sets no sign or room rule. One web search for a Grand Rapids single-user or all-gender restroom ordinance returned other cities only. City Code Chapter 131 was not read, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'.

contractor.note: From research/local-rules/cities.json (2026-11-03): 'Contractors must register their Michigan license with the City of Grand Rapids Development Center before the city issues commercial permits.' Re-read today on the city's Registered Contractor page: 'If you have a State of Michigan license and want to apply for permits in Grand Rapids, you'll need to register it with the City.' The commercial renovation permit page adds, under 'Not the owner?': 'A residential builder's license issued by the State of Michigan is needed Or a written authorization from a license holder is needed' and describes the standard as 'the Michigan residential building code', wording that looks carried over from the residential page.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Grand Rapids job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Michigan rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Grand Rapids offices, schools, hospitals and manufacturing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Michigan's plumbing rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. They apply across the state, Grand Rapids included. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Grand Rapids says a renovation of a commercial building needs a commercial building permit. Michigan's building rules, which the city enforces, list the work that needs no building permit. The list covers painting, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work, and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high that aren't fixed in place. It doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask the Grand Rapids Development Center (616-456-4100) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.install_rule: Contractors must register their Michigan license with the City of Grand Rapids Development Center before the city issues commercial permits. Michigan licenses residential builders and maintenance and alteration contractors, but has no state license for commercial interior work such as partition installation. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor with a Michigan license registers it with the Grand Rapids Development Center before applying for permits.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on schools and other public buildings paid for in whole or in part by the state, Michigan law requires at least the prevailing local wage and benefits, and contractors on those jobs must register with the state. The Kent County schedule dated November 2025 lists a journeyman carpenter at $53.30 an hour at straight time. The state issues new rates every November 1.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6% in Grand Rapids. Michigan has one statewide rate and no city or county sales tax.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and medical office buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are disinfected many times a day.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Michigan barrier free design requirements (1966 PA 1, MCL 125.1351 to 125.1356; 2021 Michigan Building Code Chapter 11; ICC A117.1-2017 except sections 611 and 707); 2021 Michigan Building Code (2021 International Building Code with Michigan amendments, R 408.30401 to R 408.30499a), effective April 9, 2025; 2021 Michigan Plumbing Code (2021 International Plumbing Code with Michigan amendments, R 408.30701 to R 408.30796), effective March 12, 2024; both apply statewide under the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act (1972 PA 230, MCL 125.1508a) and are enforced in Grand Rapids by the Development Center (Building Inspections); Section 105.2 of the building code (R 408.30409) for work exempt from permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions counts as a commercial renovation that needs a Grand Rapids building permit and sealed plans (Development Center, 616-456-4100, devcenter@grcity.us).

The city's site names no code edition: its old 'Codes Enforced by Building Inspections' page is gone (404) and its plan review checklist still cites 'MBC 2009'. The 2021 editions and dates come from the state's code page.
Grand Rapids City Code Chapter 131 (building) sits on Municode, which blocks automated reading: open it in a browser and confirm it holds nothing on toilet counts, permit-free work or restroom signs.

Public jobs rate: $53.30 is from the Kent County schedule dated November 2025. The schedule in force since November 1, 2026 sits in a Power BI viewer on the state's Prevailing Wages By County page: read the Carpenter row for Kent County in a browser and update the bullet.
The state schedule gives one straight-time figure per trade and doesn't split wages from benefits; ask the Wage and Hour Division for the split if the page should show it.

Contractor registration: the city's page speaks of contractors who hold a State of Michigan license, and Michigan has no license for commercial partition work. Ask the Development Center what an installer without a state license files, and whether the 'residential builder's license' line on the commercial renovation permit page applies to commercial jobs.

Not found, not ruled out: a Grand Rapids ordinance on single-user or all-gender restroom signs (the Human Rights Ordinance was read and has none), and a Grand Rapids wage rule for city contracts (not looked for).

Michigan is updating its plumbing rules (2024 edition, hearing held August 5, 2026; in force 120 days after filing) and its building rules (draft). No effective date is published. Recheck the stall table when the new plumbing rules are filed.
